method_card.title: Relationships and Future Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers relationships and family life vocabulary, pros and cons of marriage, and how to talk about future plans using the conditional tense.

FrenchEnglish
le couplecouple
le/la partenairepartner
le mariagemarriage / wedding
se marierto get married
le PACScivil partnership
se séparerto separate
célibatairesingle
l'amourlove
sortir avecto go out with
tomber amoureux/amoureuseto fall in love
je voudraisI would like
j'aimeraisI would like
ce seraitit would be
à l'avenirin the future

The conditional tense expresses what you would like to do. For most verbs: take the infinitive and add the imperfect endings (-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient). Common irregular stems: être → ser-, avoir → aur-, aller → ir-, faire → fer-, vouloir → voudr-. The most useful forms at GCSE are: je voudrais (I would like), j'aimerais (I would like), ce serait (it would be).

Usage: After je voudrais / j'aimerais, use an infinitive: Je voudrais me marier un jour. (I would like to get married one day.) After ce serait + adjective + de, also use an infinitive: Ce serait idéal d'habiter à la campagne. (It would be ideal to live in the countryside.)

Model paragraph: À l'avenir, je voudrais me marier et avoir deux enfants. Cependant, je pense qu'on peut être heureux sans se marier. Un PACS est plus simple et moins cher. (In the future, I would like to get married and have two children. However, I think you can be happy without getting married. A civil partnership is simpler and cheaper.)
steps: Learn the key relationship and marriage vocabulary
Practise giving pros and cons of marriage using opinion phrases
Form the conditional tense — infinitive + imperfect endings
Use je voudrais, j'aimerais and ce serait to express future plans

exam_context.frequency: Common topic in extended writing and speaking tasks

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Le mariage coûte très cher.'

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Le mariage = Marriage. coûte = costs (present tense of coûter). très cher = very expensive.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Marriage costs a lot of money. / Marriage is very expensive.

worked_examples.question: How do you form 'I would like' in French?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Take the infinitive aimer and add the imperfect ending for je: -ais.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: aimer + -ais = j'aimerais. You can also use vouloir with its irregular stem: voudr- + -ais = je voudrais.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: j'aimerais or je voudrais — both mean 'I would like' and use the conditional tense. Both are followed by an infinitive.

bronze.question: Match the French relationship vocabulary to the English meaning
Match the French phrases to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct conditional form

gaps.correct_explain: voudrais is the conditional of vouloir. Je voudrais = I would like.

wrong.vais: vais is near future (I am going to). The sentence uses 'would like', so use the conditional.
wrong.veux: veux is present tense (I want). The sentence needs the conditional: voudrais.

gaps.correct_explain: avoir is the infinitive — after je voudrais, use the infinitive form.

wrong.ai: ai is conjugated present tense. After voudrais, use the infinitive avoir.

gaps.correct_explain: engagement = commitment. Un engagement sérieux = a serious commitment.
tradition = tradition. Une tradition importante = an important tradition.

bronze.question: What does 'Ce n'est pas nécessaire — on peut être heureux sans se marier' mean?
options: It is not necessary — you can be happy without getting married
It is necessary to be happy before getting married
It is not possible to be happy without a marriage
They are not happy because they got married

bronze.question: Which sentence uses the conditional tense correctly?
options: Je vais habiter à la campagne

bronze.source_text: Beaucoup de mariages finissent par un divorce. On peut choisir un PACS, qui est plus simple.
model_answers: Many marriages end in divorce. You can choose a PACS (civil partnership), which is simpler.

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct conditional form
silver.english: It would be ideal to live in the countryside.

gaps.correct_explain: serait is the conditional of être. Irregular stem: ser- + -ait.

wrong.est: est is present tense. 'It would be' requires the conditional: serait.
wrong.sera: sera is the simple future. The conditional needs serait (with -ait).

gaps.correct_explain: habiter is the infinitive — ce serait idéal d'habiter = it would be ideal to live.

wrong.habite: habite is conjugated. After de, use the infinitive habiter.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Elle est tombé amoureuse de son partenaire l'année dernière.
silver.explanation: Elle is feminine, and tomber uses être in the perfect tense. The past participle must agree with the subject: tombée (add -e for feminine).
silver.translation: She fell in love with her partner last year.

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: In the future, I would like to get married.

distractor_labels.veux: wrong tense — veux is present (I want), not conditional (I would like). Use voudrais

silver.source_text: I would like to get married but marriage is very expensive.
model_answers: Je voudrais me marier mais le mariage coûte très cher.
J'aimerais me marier mais le mariage est très cher.

gold.source_text: When I am older, I would like to get married and have children. However, I think that you can be happy without getting married. A civil partnership is simpler and cheaper.
model_answers: Quand je serai plus âgé(e), je voudrais me marier et avoir des enfants. Cependant, je pense qu'on peut être heureux sans se marier. Un PACS est plus simple et moins cher.

gold.question: Build the sentence in French
gold.english: I would like my partner to be kind and honest.

distractor_labels.est: wrong mood — after aimerais que, French requires the subjunctive soit, not the indicative est
distractor_labels.serait: wrong mood — after que, you need the subjunctive soit, not the conditional serait
distractor_labels.ma: wrong gender — partenaire is used as masculine here, so mon is correct

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a café with a French exchange student. They ask about your views on relationships and future plans.

bullets.prompt: Give your opinion on marriage — say one advantage.
bullets.model_answer: À mon avis, le mariage est une belle célébration de l'amour et montre un engagement sérieux.
bullets.note: opinion phrase + vocabulary: engagement, amour, célébration

bullets.model_answer: Cependant, le mariage coûte très cher et beaucoup de mariages finissent par un divorce.
bullets.note: cependant = however; coûter cher; finir par + noun

bullets.prompt: Say what you would like to do in the future regarding relationships.
bullets.model_answer: À l'avenir, je voudrais me marier et avoir deux enfants. J'aimerais habiter à la campagne.
bullets.note: conditional: voudrais, aimerais + infinitive; à l'avenir
